LMS: schedule, ledger and exact money

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Distinguish schedule from ledger
  • Explain exact-paise accounting
  • Reconstruct a balance

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Disbursement event
  2. 02Contract schedule
  3. 03Accrual events
  4. 04Payment allocation
  5. 05Charges / reversals
  6. 06Derived balance
  7. 07Statement

1. Account opening

Successful disbursement opens the LMS account with contractual principal, rate, tenor and schedule rules. Schedule rows describe expected cash flows; ledger events record what actually happened.

2. Exact money

Domain values use integer paise or validated decimal strings at boundaries.

Interest, allocation, charges, waivers and reversals have explicit rounding.

Floating point is prohibited on Rust evaluation paths.

3. Reconstruction

Balance is derived from ordered, immutable ledger events. Payment allocation, accrual, prepayment, foreclosure and correction events preserve lineage; destructive editing would make statements and audit replay unreliable.
